# Empire AI Agency — Real-Customer Connector Owner Release Gate

23 October 2026 | One existing EmpireOS agency delivery engine | Release decision: HOLD

## Canonical system boundary

The existing *agency car-yard feature branch* now has actual read-only MCP ↔ WordPress/MariaDB and original PostgreSQL 041 membership checks, an owner-gated preflight, independent owner/security signature verification and single-host replay receipts.

**This is not production authorisation.** All current signed site-owner and connector-security records are generated by offline synthetic tests; there is no verified real customer site-to-tenant grant or approved production issuer installed in the branch. The guarded MCP demo remains staging-only. The actual canonical tenant/CRM identity reader is already implemented; do not create a parallel identity database or borrow its credentials without its owner's authorisation.

## Required owner-supplied evidence (independent of our test fixtures)

| Owner | Required source and sign-off | Acceptance, before any launcher can start |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Canonical EmpireDB/CRM tenant owner | Approved agency-purpose, minimum-privilege membership reader for a named test tenant and identity; scope, revoke/read semantics, approved DSN custody | Fresh bounded read using the existing 041 membership authority; no general CRM token and no extra live grants from this branch |
| Client/WordPress site owner | Independently verified authority over exact WordPress installation; site identifier, tenant binding, legal/site consent, permitted read operations, expiration, revocation route | Attested first-party site ownership, named reviewer/approval receipt, allowed read-only inventory/capability tools; not just a DNS URL or self-asserted JWT |
| Connector security owner | Separate approval for connector ID, hostname and TLS/origin binding, scopes, data field allowlist, source rights and revocation | Separately signed grant against exactly the same tenant/site/credential reference; no bookings, payment, CRM or outbound permissions |
| Identity and key-custody owner | Separately provisioned and revocable agency-audience issuer, site-owner and connector-security public key roster; signing-key rotation and provenance | Keys remain distinct; issuer and key approval come from an independent owner, not an agent-generated keypair |
| Credential owner | Approved per-tenant/per-site credential delivery and rotation, immediate revoke, protected runtime identity and at-rest custody | Service-owned vault/systemd credential integration confirmed with actual mode semantics and test credential only; no commit/env fallback/public HTTP |
| Security/ops release owner | Reproducible test-tenant E2E, auditable per-call authorisation, replay storage and transport validation | Approved launcher uses owner-gated preflight on **each MCP tool**, rejects stale/revoked grants and DB membership, proves no WordPress request after denial |
| Founder release owner | Final explicit publication/production approval after above evidence is independently read back | No deployment, customer data, outbound, payment or public booking before this last gate |

## Architecture decision and the missing interface

The correct consumer is already **empire_os.agency_owner_gated_connector.OwnerGatedAgencyConnector**. It composes canonical membership, independent signed site and connector grants, nonce replay receipts and restricted credential resolution. The Node MCP revocation guard must call this trusted owner-controlled service before every read. The existing local Python-to-Node authority bridge was only a test harness and must not be used with production customer data.

The signers are **not** created by the consumer. Never treat the JSON test registry, fixtures, file presence, environment variables or signing keys generated during tests as production approval. The existing protected EmpireDB reader must not be invoked by a newly created agency service until its canonical owner approves service identity and credential scope.

## Current evidence and what it proves

- Commit `1cd154cea`: combined original PostgreSQL migration 041, authenticated real WordPress REST + MariaDB, MCP guard and private bridge. Eight real-engine **synthetic** tests passed, including revocation mid-session.
- Commit `4d35000ea`: two independently signed test approvals and persistent single-host nonce receipts. 167 Python tests passed, two skipped; eleven MCP protocol/policy tests passed.
- All signing keys, site ownership claims, credentials and membership records used to test the grant flows were fictional, short-lived and isolated.
- No live EmpireDB membership read/write, actual site owner consent, permanent security issuer, vault integration, OAuth service, remote MCP deployment or production/customer activation was established.

## Next executable milestone (owner-controlled)

Use a named, authorised non-customer **test tenant** in the already existing EmpireOS tenant authority. Obtain read-only service access approval from the canonical owner, establish site-owner and connector-security approvals through their separately owned signing service, and provision approved credentials into a dedicated isolated service identity. Then replace the synthetic provider inputs in the joined test with independently read-back owner inputs, run negative cross-tenant/expired/revoked/rotated-credential tests, and present the results for founder release approval.

Until those inputs are independently verified: **HOLD — read-only offline tests only.** No second CRM, no Supabase, no paid traffic, no production service changes.
